# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

Description ## Problem The review prompt orders maximal recall, and the machine converts findings into rework laps (any ⚠️ → REQUEST_CHANGES under the `default` preset). Two measured pathologies: 1. **Findings on already-reviewed code** — `general_guidelines.md` §3 ("read the full content of every changed file") re-exposes all old code every round; §7 (*"Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration"*) rewards reporting anything improvable anywhere in it. 2. **Fix-of-finding creates new findings** — the rework's fresh hunks get the same maximality treatment, so each lap mints new ⚠️s on its own fix. Severity inflation is instructed too (§6: *"When in doubt, start one level higher"*). ## The research caveat that shapes this issue Springer, *Automated Software Engineering* 33:90 (2026) — "Are LLMs reliable code reviewers? Systematic overcorrection in requirement conformance judgement": LLM reviewers systematically over-correct, and **richer prompts amplify it** — requiring explanations + proposed fixes drove GPT-4o's false-rejection of correct code from 26% to 73–88%. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10515-026-00638-5 So this is NOT "add more instructions/expectations". It is a **decision-rule swap**: change what earns a finding, do not add detail. The industry postmortem behind the same rule (12 fix-review rounds in 2 h, 209 conversations, ~90% individually accurate — accuracy was the problem): https://aq.dev/guides/ai-code-review-noise/ ## Planned changes (all in `instructions/pr_review/*` + one input file) 1. **Necessity test replaces §7 maximality**: a finding earns a thread only if it defends correctness on a path the change actually touches, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract. Accurate-but-not-merge-relevant → ranked digest, never a thread. Drop "maximum number of findings"; state the cost ("each thread costs a lap, 15–20 CI minutes"). 2. **Frozen already-reviewed code (pathology 1)**: re-review rounds review the **diff-of-diff** (new hunks since the last reviewed head) + the interaction neighborhood, not whole files. Unchanged lines are frozen: a finding there requires the new hunks to make it worse (interaction test), otherwise it is advisory digest only. Machine provides `pr_new_hunks.txt` so the rule is cheap to follow. 3. **Anti-inflation swap in §6**: "when in doubt, start one level higher" → "when in doubt, classify lower and state what evidence would raise it" (the existing external-spec citation rule, generalized). 4. **Delegate to the gates**: complexity/duplication/style are already measured by repo CI (crap ratchet, duplication gate, lint) — findings there only if the gate is missing and the cost is concrete. ## Sequencing Ship and measure this BEFORE the filter leg (#1403) if possible: it is zero-quota, and it shrinks the candidate pool the filter would verify (filter cost is per candidate). Cross-linked so trial attribution stays clean: prompt change and filter leg must not land together unmeasured. ## Guards - Prompt text changes only the decision rule; severity definitions, verdict mapping, output contracts stay as-is (the machine recomputes the verdict from the census — gh-1351 — and is untouched). - Effect is measured with the same Outdated-Rate KPI as #1403 (from gh-1332 dispositions). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile…","blocks":[{"type":"text","chars":13961,"text":"# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents ## Architecture This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts. ### Execution model 1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows. 2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist: - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result) - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI) - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation 3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic. ### Key layers | Layer | Location | Purpose | |-------|----------|---------| | SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing | | Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) | | JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic | | Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic | | Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults | | Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents | | Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) | | Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup | ## GraalJS Constraints All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js. - Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals). - No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages. - No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`. - Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`. - Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo. - **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one. - Keep data structures JSON-safe. ## Running Tests Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed. ```bash # Run from the dmtools-agents repo root cd dmtools-agents # All tests dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # Single test suite dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json ``` Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`). ### Writing tests for new logic **All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.** - Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_.js` file. - Add it to the corresponding `run_.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`. - Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module. - Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services. - Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config. - Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context. Example mock pattern: ```js var fileReadMock = function(opts) { var p = opts && (opts.path || opts); if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p]; if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; } }; ``` ### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring (preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible: 1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run --key value` patches the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden: ```bash dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \ --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \ --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \ --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \ --alwaysPostComments false \ --cleanupInputFolder false ``` 2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g. `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is project- and machine-specific): ```bash #!/bin/bash set -e mkdir -p outputs printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md ``` Rules for live e2e runs: - **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything via CLI overrides. - Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items. - Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input//` afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet. - After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`, `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather than trusting the job log. ## Conventions ### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE **This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite. Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages): - Company, customer, or product names - Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys - Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization - File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs - Sample data copied from real internal systems Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION / NIT
(severity census gates approval per review_policy.md)"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_findings.md — previously raised findings (when present)"] P8["8️⃣ input/TICKET/review_policy.md — the resolved reviewPolicy: severity table, density cap, downgrade protocol (gh-1351)"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 --> P8 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement to the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Does not block merge. - **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Never blocks merge, never triggers a lap. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### Density control — post top-K, digest the overflow (gh-1351) `review_policy.md` in the input folder carries the resolved policy and its density cap (`allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8)` — 20→3 · 50→4 · 200→5 · 800→8): - The cap applies to 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT threads only — 🚨/⚠️ findings are **never capped** and always post as threads. - Rank your 💡/🪶 findings by value and post only the top-K as inline threads. - The overflow becomes a **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`). - The census counts posted threads + digest lines (`issueCounts.suggestions`/`nits` count posts, `digest` counts the overflow lines). - The machine audits the posted thread count against the cap (warn only — it never fails the leg). ### Downgrade protocol — honor a justified ⚠️→💡 from rework (gh-1351) A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification in the census** (its thread reply and response summary). When the justification is present, classify the finding 💡 in this round's census — a false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. A silent downgrade does not exist: without the written justification, keep ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - **Before emitting a spec-claim finding without a citation, locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it (for example `ticket.md:12`) — an uncited true claim is demoted mechanically.** - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. The machine applies the same discipline (and a safety net against coin-flip formatting): every uncited spec claim is cross-checked against the ticket text the run already has under `input/`. When the requirement is verifiably present there, the finding keeps 🚨 BLOCKING force and the matched citation is auto-appended; when the ticket contradicts it, lacks it, or the mechanical check is inconclusive, the finding is demoted and stamped `demoted-from-BLOCKING` — the finding-identity registry keeps it re-elevatable in a later round by adding a citation instead of raising the same defect as new. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## 9. Previously raised findings — the finding-identity registry When `input/TICKET/pr_findings.md` is present, earlier review rounds on this PR already raised findings **F1–Fn** (each with its claim, file and status). The registry dedup is what keeps repeated rounds from minting duplicate threads for the same defect. Answer the registry **before** raising anything new: - **verify fixed** — the fixing hunk you can cite closes the finding: disposition `"fixed"` with the hunk reference. Never mark `fixed` without a citable hunk. - **withdraw (reason required)** — the claim is wrong or no longer applies: disposition `"withdrawn"` with the reason. A withdrawal without a reason is rejected by the machine, and BLOCKING withdrawals surface to the owner. - **mark re-introduced** — the defect is still there (e.g. the fix was reverted): leave the finding open and let your re-raise match it; do not re-litigate the claim from scratch. New claims always need new evidence. A finding on the registry list is answered, not re-raised as if it were news — and the reviewer instruction stays maximally ambitious: raise every actionable finding you actually see. **Candidates pending confirmation** (also listed in `pr_findings.md`): when a new finding you raised is *possibly same as F*, the machine asks one word per candidate — confirm with `"same as F"` or call it `"new"`. Unconfirmed candidates become new identities; nothing merges without your confirmation. This is a dedup request, not a push-back: confirming merges the threads, it does not weaken the finding (merges can only escalate severity, never de-escalate). Add a `findingReview` block to `outputs/pr_review.json` (alongside `inlineComments`): ```json {"findingReview": { "dispositions": [ {"n": 1, "status": "fixed", "hunk": "src/auth.ts:40-48 — try/catch added"}, {"n": 2, "status": "withdrawn", "reason": "validation exists at src/auth.ts:50 — claim was wrong"}, {"n": 3, "status": "re-introduced"} ], "confirmations": [ {"proposedFor": 1, "same": true} ] }} ``` When `pr_findings.md` is absent, this section does not apply — review exactly as before.

# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed (gh-1351, 4 tiers):

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — clarity of the documented/behavioral surface:
  missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape.
- 🪶 **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style,
  formatting, naming micro-preferences.

Then map to the verdict (the machine recomputes it from the census —
`postPRReviewComments` treats your token as advisory):

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| Any ⚠️ IMPORTANT (no 🚨) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` (gates approval — policy default) |
| Only 💡 / 🪶 remain | `APPROVE` — the cycle converges |

**Downgrade protocol (gh-1351):** when the rework lap downgraded a specific ⚠️ to 💡 **with a
written justification in the census** (the thread reply states why the finding is not
maintainability debt), classify that finding 💡 in this round's census — the false-⚠️ review
converges to APPROVE without a code change. Without the written justification, keep ⚠️: a silent
downgrade does not exist, and the machine recomputes the verdict from the census you post.

`APPROVE` with remaining 💡/🪶 findings is the expected terminal state
(the resolved policy's `allowApproveWithSuggestions` derives from the
tier table — SUGGESTION rounds polish, NIT rounds none): post every
remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do
**not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round.
An open ⚠️ **does** gate approval unless the project's `reviewPolicy`
explicitly weakens it (owner standing-approval doctrine, epic §4.4).

## Anti-patterns

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, doc-comment refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X"
  without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read).
  Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as
  ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also
  downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with
  the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.)
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from a release bump or pin PR strands that PR behind the standard queue.
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

function trimLargeTextForInput(content, label, maxChars) {
    var text = content || '';
    var limit = maxChars || MAX_PR_DIFF_CONTEXT_CHARS;
    if (text.length <= limit) return text;

    var headChars = Math.floor(limit * 0.65);
    var tailChars = limit - headChars;
    return [
        '# ' + label + ' Truncated',
        '',
        'Original size: ' + text.length + ' characters.',
        'Kept: first ' + headChars + ' and last ' + tailChars + ' characters.',
        '',
        'The full diff is available in the checked-out PR branch. Use `git diff` or CodeGraph for focused source navigation instead of relying only on this file.',
        '',
        '```diff',
        text.substring(0, headChars),
        '',
        '... [' + (text.length - limit) + ' characters omitted] ...',
        '',
        text.substring(text.length - tailChars),
        '```'
    ].join('\n');
}

function writeInputFile(path, content, label) {
    var text = content || '';
    console.log('Writing ' + label + ' to ' + path + ' (' + text.length + ' chars)');
    file_write({ path: path, content: text });
    console.log('Wrote ' + label + ' to ' + path);
}

/**
 * Write PR context files to input folder.
 * Writes: pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json
 *
 * @param {string}      inputFolder  - input/{ticketKey} path
 * @param {Object}      prDetails    - PR object (GitHub or GitLab, normalized)
 * @param {string}      diff         - git diff text
 * @param {string|null} markdown     - discussions markdown (from githubHelpers.fetchDiscussionsAndRawData)
 * @param {Object|null} rawThreads   - raw threads with IDs (from githubHelpers.fetchDiscussionsAndRawData)
 */
/**
 * gh-806 AC4 + gh-957 AC3: serialize the open threads (already-resolved ones
 * filtered out — a rework/review leg must not spend a duplicate reply pass on
 * closed conversations) WITH the GraphQL census riding along (arm-rule
 * unresolved count + trusted-author breakdown) — the rework leg's input and
 * the SM arm's threads count stay the SAME source.
 */
function writeDiscussionsRawJson(inputFolder, rawThreads) {
    var allThreads = (rawThreads.threads || []);
    var openThreads = allThreads.filter(function(t) { return !!t && t.resolved !== true; });
    if (openThreads.length !== allThreads.length) {
        console.log('Filtered ' + (allThreads.length - openThreads.length) +
            ' already-resolved thread(s) out of pr_discussions_raw.json (gh-806 AC4)');
    }
    writeInputFile(
        inputFolder + '/pr_discussions_raw.json',
        JSON.stringify({ threads: openThreads, census: rawThreads.census || null }, null, 2),
        'pr_discussions_raw.json (' + openThreads.length + ' threads)'
    );
}

#!/bin/sh
# Pre-commit hook: auto-regenerate agent snapshots when agent configs or MD files change.
#
# Install:
#   ./scripts/install-hooks.sh
#   (or manually: git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks)

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
SNAPSHOT_SCRIPT="$REPO_ROOT/generate_agent_snapshots.js"
SNAPSHOTS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/snapshots"

# Check if any staged files are JSON configs, MD instructions, or the generator itself
# (added/copied/modified only — deleted files must not trip the human-doc check)
STAGED_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM)

NEEDS_REGEN=false
for f in $STAGED_FILES; do
    case "$f" in
        *.json|*.md|generate_agent_snapshots.js|scripts/hooks/*)
            NEEDS_REGEN=true
            break
            ;;
    esac
done

if [ "$NEEDS_REGEN" = "false" ]; then
    exit 0
fi

if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "⚠️  node not found. Skipping snapshot regeneration."
    exit 0
fi

echo "🔄 Regenerating agent snapshots..."
node "$SNAPSHOT_SCRIPT"
EXIT_CODE=$?

if [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ Snapshot generation failed. Fix errors above and retry."
    exit 1
fi

# Stage any updated snapshots so they are included in the same commit
UPDATED_SNAPSHOTS=$(git diff --name-only "$SNAPSHOTS_DIR" 2>/dev/null)
UNTRACKED_SNAPSHOTS=$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard "$SNAPSHOTS_DIR" 2>/dev/null)

if [ -n "$UPDATED_SNAPSHOTS" ] || [ -n "$UNTRACKED_SNAPSHOTS" ]; then
    git add "$SNAPSHOTS_DIR"
    echo "✅ Snapshots regenerated and staged automatically."
    if [ -n "$UPDATED_SNAPSHOTS" ]; then
        echo "   Modified:"
        echo "$UPDATED_SNAPSHOTS" | sed 's/^/      /'
    fi
    if [ -n "$UNTRACKED_SNAPSHOTS" ]; then
        echo "   New:"
        echo "$UNTRACKED_SNAPSHOTS" | sed 's/^/      /'
    fi
fi

# ── Agent docs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Regenerate docs/agents/generated/* whenever agent configs, JS actions,
# instructions, prompts, human docs, or the generator itself change.

DOC_GENERATOR="$REPO_ROOT/js/agentDocGenerator.js"
DOCS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/docs/agents"

NEEDS_DOC_REGEN=false
for f in $STAGED_FILES; do
    case "$f" in
        *.json|js/*.js|js/common/*.js|instructions/*|prompts/*|docs/agents/*.md|js/agentDocGenerator.js)
            NEEDS_DOC_REGEN=true
            break
            ;;
    esac
done

if [ "$NEEDS_DOC_REGEN" = "true" ]; then
    echo "🔄 Regenerating agent docs..."
    node "$DOC_GENERATOR"
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "❌ Agent docs generation failed. Fix errors above and retry."
        exit 1
    fi
    UPDATED_DOCS=$(git diff --name-only "$DOCS_DIR" 2>/dev/null)
    UNTRACKED_DOCS=$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard "$DOCS_DIR" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$UPDATED_DOCS" ] || [ -n "$UNTRACKED_DOCS" ]; then
        git add "$DOCS_DIR"
        echo "✅ Agent docs regenerated and staged automatically."
    fi

    # A changed/new agent config needs a human doc at docs/agents/<name>.md —
    # the docs coverage unit test enforces this in CI; fail early here.
    for f in $STAGED_FILES; do
        case "$f" in
            *.json)
                base=$(basename "$f" .json)
                case "$base" in
                    sm|sm_merge|run_*|*_lock) continue ;;
                esac
                case "$f" in
                    */*) continue ;;  # only root agent configs
                esac
                if [ ! -s "$REPO_ROOT/docs/agents/$base.md" ]; then
                    echo "❌ Missing human doc: docs/agents/$base.md"
                    echo "   Add a 1-2 sentence description of what the agent does"
                    echo "   plus a Parameters section (see other docs/agents/*.md)."
                    exit 1
                fi
                ;;
        esac
    done
fi

exit 0

arguments.newText:
## 3. Changed-file deep read — and frozen already-reviewed code

Do not review from the diff alone.

**First review round** (no `pr_new_hunks.txt` in the input folder) — read the full content of every changed file:

- imports and dependencies
- class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles
- naming consistency with the rest of the codebase
- error handling, logging, and edge cases
- test coverage for changed behavior
- backward-compatibility and migration impact

**Re-review rounds** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` present — the hunks added since the last reviewed head) — read the full content of the files the new hunks touch plus their interaction neighborhood (direct callers/callees of changed symbols), not whole files. Already-reviewed lines are **frozen**: a finding on an unchanged line is valid only when the new hunks make the problem worse (the interaction test — e.g. a new call path now feeds unvalidated input into old code). Anything else on frozen lines is advisory digest at most (§7), never a thread. If `pr_new_hunks.txt` is absent from a later round (e.g. a force-push the machine could not diff), the whole diff is in scope again.

arguments.newText:
## 7. Necessity test — what earns a thread

A thread is expensive: each one costs a rework lap — 15–20 CI minutes — and the rework's own fresh hunks get reviewed again next round. A finding earns a thread only if it **defends** one of:

- correctness on a path the change actually touches
- security
- data loss
- CI breakage
- the ticket contract

Everything else — real, accurate, but not merge-relevant — goes to the **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`), never a thread.

- Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists — classify everything you found; only the necessity test decides thread vs digest.
- The exhaustive pass keeps running (§3 defines its scope). Re-read the in-scope code and ask: *"What else does this change put at risk?"* — not *"What else is improvable here?"*
- Before writing outputs, verify each thread you are about to open passes the necessity test; everything else is already in the digest.

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Deep read:
first round — every changed file;
re-review (pr_new_hunks.txt present) —
new hunks + interaction neighborhood
(unchanged lines frozen)"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION / NIT
(severity census gates approval per review_policy.md)"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Necessity pass:
threads only for findings that defend
correctness / security / data loss / CI / ticket contract —
everything else → ranked digest"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_findings.md — previously raised findings (when present)"] P8["8️⃣ input/TICKET/review_policy.md — the resolved reviewPolicy: severity table, density cap, downgrade protocol (gh-1351)"] P9["9️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_new_hunks.txt — the hunks added since the last reviewed head (re-review rounds; when present)"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 --> P8 --> P9 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: does each candidate finding pass the §7 necessity test (defends correctness on a touched path, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract) — or is it digest material? ## 3. Changed-file deep read — and frozen already-reviewed code Do not review from the diff alone. **First review round** (no `pr_new_hunks.txt` in the input folder) — read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact **Re-review rounds** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` present — the hunks added since the last reviewed head) — read the full content of the files the new hunks touch plus their interaction neighborhood (direct callers/callees of changed symbols), not whole files. Already-reviewed lines are **frozen**: a finding on an unchanged line is valid only when the new hunks make the problem worse (the interaction test — e.g. a new call path now feeds unvalidated input into old code). Anything else on frozen lines is advisory digest at most (§7), never a thread. If `pr_new_hunks.txt` is absent from a later round (e.g. a force-push the machine could not diff), the whole diff is in scope again. ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ### Delegate to the measured gates (gh-1404) Complexity, duplication and style are already measured by the repo's CI — the CRAP ratchet, the duplication gate, lint. The gate is the reviewer of record for those dimensions: a passing gate is not a thread (the cost was already measured and accepted); a failing gate is CI breakage (🚨 BLOCKING). Raise a complexity/duplication/style finding only when no gate covers it **and** the concrete cost is stateable — what breaks or what the next change pays. ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement to the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Does not block merge. - **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Never blocks merge, never triggers a lap. When in doubt, classify lower and state what evidence would raise the finding one level (the same discipline as the external-spec citation rule below — an unproven claim must not hold a PR hostage). ### Density control — post top-K, digest the overflow (gh-1351) `review_policy.md` in the input folder carries the resolved policy and its density cap (`allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8)` — 20→3 · 50→4 · 200→5 · 800→8): - The cap applies to 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT threads only — 🚨/⚠️ findings are **never capped** and always post as threads. - Rank your 💡/🪶 findings by value and post only the top-K as inline threads. - The overflow becomes a **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`). - The census counts posted threads + digest lines (`issueCounts.suggestions`/`nits` count posts, `digest` counts the overflow lines). - The machine audits the posted thread count against the cap (warn only — it never fails the leg). ### Downgrade protocol — honor a justified ⚠️→💡 from rework (gh-1351) A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification in the census** (its thread reply and response summary). When the justification is present, classify the finding 💡 in this round's census — a false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. A silent downgrade does not exist: without the written justification, keep ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - **Before emitting a spec-claim finding without a citation, locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it (for example `ticket.md:12`) — an uncited true claim is demoted mechanically.** - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. The machine applies the same discipline (and a safety net against coin-flip formatting): every uncited spec claim is cross-checked against the ticket text the run already has under `input/`. When the requirement is verifiably present there, the finding keeps 🚨 BLOCKING force and the matched citation is auto-appended; when the ticket contradicts it, lacks it, or the mechanical check is inconclusive, the finding is demoted and stamped `demoted-from-BLOCKING` — the finding-identity registry keeps it re-elevatable in a later round by adding a citation instead of raising the same defect as new. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Necessity test — what earns a thread A thread is expensive: each one costs a rework lap — 15–20 CI minutes — and the rework's own fresh hunks get reviewed again next round. A finding earns a thread only if it **defends** one of: - correctness on a path the change actually touches - security - data loss - CI breakage - the ticket contract Everything else — real, accurate, but not merge-relevant — goes to the **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`), never a thread. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists — classify everything you found; only the necessity test decides thread vs digest. - The exhaustive pass keeps running (§3 defines its scope). Re-read the in-scope code and ask: *"What else does this change put at risk?"* — not *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify each thread you are about to open passes the necessity test; everything else is already in the digest. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## 9. Previously raised findings — the finding-identity registry When `input/TICKET/pr_findings.md` is present, earlier review rounds on this PR already raised findings **F1–Fn** (each with its claim, file and status). The registry dedup is what keeps repeated rounds from minting duplicate threads for the same defect. Answer the registry **before** raising anything new: - **verify fixed** — the fixing hunk you can cite closes the finding: disposition `"fixed"` with the hunk reference. Never mark `fixed` without a citable hunk. - **withdraw (reason required)** — the claim is wrong or no longer applies: disposition `"withdrawn"` with the reason. A withdrawal without a reason is rejected by the machine, and BLOCKING withdrawals surface to the owner. - **mark re-introduced** — the defect is still there (e.g. the fix was reverted): leave the finding open and let your re-raise match it; do not re-litigate the claim from scratch. New claims always need new evidence, and they pass the same §7 necessity test before they earn a thread. A finding on the registry list is answered, not re-raised as if it were news. **Candidates pending confirmation** (also listed in `pr_findings.md`): when a new finding you raised is *possibly same as F*, the machine asks one word per candidate — confirm with `"same as F"` or call it `"new"`. Unconfirmed candidates become new identities; nothing merges without your confirmation. This is a dedup request, not a push-back: confirming merges the threads, it does not weaken the finding (merges can only escalate severity, never de-escalate). Add a `findingReview` block to `outputs/pr_review.json` (alongside `inlineComments`): ```json {"findingReview": { "dispositions": [ {"n": 1, "status": "fixed", "hunk": "src/auth.ts:40-48 — try/catch added"}, {"n": 2, "status": "withdrawn", "reason": "validation exists at src/auth.ts:50 — claim was wrong"}, {"n": 3, "status": "re-introduced"} ], "confirmations": [ {"proposedFor": 1, "same": true} ] }} ``` When `pr_findings.md` is absent, this section does not apply — review exactly as before.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Duplication gate (gh-1251): a second, independent gate fails PRs and main on
# NEW or GROWING JS duplication. The measurement is
# `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci`; a
# pinned set of production files already exceeds 1% today (pre-existing debt
# owned by the gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets — see duplication-baseline.json
# for the current pinned set), so the gate is a RATCHET against that
# baseline, not an absolute bar — it fails only when a file over threshold is
# not pinned or a pinned file gained ABSOLUTE duplicated lines
# (ci/duplicationRatchet.js; percentage shifts from file shrinkage are
# informational, not failures). Its clones-mode report also feeds the README
# `duplication` endpoint badge published from the same run.
#
# Runtime-artifact guard (gh-1365): two read-only `git ls-files` queries over the
# checked-out INDEX (no working-dir state involved — robust on PR checkouts and
# dirty runner workspaces) hard-fail the job when pipeline-owned runtime artifacts
# are tracked: (1) a tracked file matching the checked-in gitignore-style pattern
# list ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt — extend THAT file, not this workflow; (2)
# a file matching .gitignore but still tracked — the missed-cleanup signature of
# the gh-1358/.dmtools-target-workingdir incident. A modified TRACKED artifact
# blocks every dev-leg checkout; untracked+ignored copies are harmless by
# construction.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']

  unchanged lines are frozen unless the new hunks make a problem worse.

arguments.content:
### What changed

Swapped the PR-review prompt's finding decision rules (gh-1404): §7 maximality is replaced by a necessity test (a thread must defend correctness on a touched path, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract — everything else goes to the ranked digest), re-review rounds now review the **diff-of-diff** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` = hunks since the last reviewed head) with unchanged lines frozen (interaction test), §6 anti-inflation ("classify lower + state what would raise it"), and complexity/duplication/style findings delegate to the measured CI gates.

### Key decisions

- Decision-rule swap, not detail-add: severity definitions (`review_verdict_rules.md`), verdict mapping and output contracts untouched — the gh-1351 census recomputation is unmodified.
- The machine provides the new input file: `js/common/prNewHunks.js` derives the last reviewed head from the newest trusted machine verdict record (`reviewVerdicts`, gh-807); `gitOps.getDiffBetweenCommits` runs one plain two-SHA diff.
- Graceful degradation end to end: first round, unchanged head, force-push (SHA missing), failed diff or provider without `getPrComments` → no file, full-diff review exactly as before (`preparePRForReview.js` step 6.6, non-fatal).
- `pr_new_hunks.txt` carries the frozen-lines contract in its header, so the rule is cheap to follow at review time.

### How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_prNewHunks.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_preparePRForReview.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_gitOps.json
```

<details><summary>Diff-of-diff flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Re-review round starts] --> V{Newest trusted verdict record on PR?}
    V -->|none — first round| F[Full-diff review, no file]
    V -->|head H| D{Current head ≠ H?}
    D -->|no| F
    D -->|yes| G[git diff H..current] --> W[Write pr_new_hunks.txt] --> RV[Review new hunks + interaction neighborhood; unchanged lines frozen → digest]
```

</details>

content.text:
### What changed

Swapped the PR-review prompt's finding decision rules (gh-1404): §7 maximality is replaced by a necessity test (a thread must defend correctness on a touched path, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract — everything else goes to the ranked digest), re-review rounds now review the **diff-of-diff** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` = hunks since the last reviewed head) with unchanged lines frozen (interaction test), §6 anti-inflation ("classify lower + state what would raise it"), and complexity/duplication/style findings delegate to the measured CI gates.

### Key decisions

- Decision-rule swap, not detail-add: severity definitions (`review_verdict_rules.md`), verdict mapping and output contracts untouched — the gh-1351 census recomputation is unmodified.
- The machine provides the new input file: `js/common/prNewHunks.js` derives the last reviewed head from the newest trusted machine verdict record (`reviewVerdicts`, gh-807); `gitOps.getDiffBetweenCommits` runs one plain two-SHA diff.
- Graceful degradation end to end: first round, unchanged head, force-push (SHA missing), failed diff or provider without `getPrComments` → no file, full-diff review exactly as before (`preparePRForReview.js` step 6.6, non-fatal).
- `pr_new_hunks.txt` carries the frozen-lines contract in its header, so the rule is cheap to follow at review time.

### How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_prNewHunks.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_preparePRForReview.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_gitOps.json
```

<details><summary>Diff-of-diff flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Re-review round starts] --> V{Newest trusted verdict record on PR?}
    V -->|none — first round| F[Full-diff review, no file]
    V -->|head H| D{Current head ≠ H?}
    D -->|no| F
    D -->|yes| G[git diff H..current] --> W[Write pr_new_hunks.txt] --> RV[Review new hunks + interaction neighborhood; unchanged lines frozen → digest]
```

</details>
===
OK: no closing keywords

empty comment list → null (first review round)' free-form review text without the marker → null (never consulted)' one machine verdict record → its head' multiple records → the NEWEST one wins (order by at, not by position)' a forged record (non-machine author) is invisible' null/undefined comment payload → null' missing last reviewed head → false (never a re-review)' missing current head → false' identical heads → false (re-review of the same code — everything frozen)' prefix-equal heads (full sha vs short sha) → false' different heads → true' a short prefix that is NOT the other head → true' header cites both heads and carries the frozen-lines contract' an empty delta still builds a file — the head moved with no code change' === 44: DIFF --> FILES["3. Deep read:
first round — every changed file;
re-review (pr_new_hunks.txt present) —
new hunks + interaction neighborhood
(unchanged lines frozen)"] 67: P9["9️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_new_hunks.txt — the hunks added since the last reviewed head (re-review rounds; when present)"] 102:## 3. Changed-file deep read — and frozen already-reviewed code 106:**First review round** (no `pr_new_hunks.txt` in the input folder) — read the full content of every changed file: 115:**Re-review rounds** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` present — the hunks added since the last reviewed head) — read the full content of the files the new hunks touch plus their interaction neighborhood (direct callers/callees of changed symbols), not whole files. Already-reviewed lines are **frozen**: a finding on an unchanged line is valid only when the new hunks make the problem worse (the interaction test — e.g. a new call path now feeds unvalidated input into old code). Anything else on frozen lines is advisory digest at most (§7), never a thread. If `pr_new_hunks.txt` is absent from a later round (e.g. a force-push the machine could not diff), the whole diff is in scope again. 510: B5["Verification order: finalize ALL code edits BEFORE launching a long verification run (full suite, coverage) — verification must run against a frozen tree, otherwise the run is wasted"]
